context: The predeclared §23.1 selection term 'settlement success' was found
underspecified after observing the ambiguity: under concrete
failure-locus attribution it selects Arm A, under concrete +
honest unknown it selects Arm D.

adjudication.definition: locus when the answer key has a determinate locus, OR
honest 'unknown' when the answer key is 'unknown'.
adjudication.reason: diagnostic decision success is the intended meaning for
choosing the retrieval substrate used by the §23.2
diagnostic-loop experiment; the corpus includes 'unknown' as a
legitimate ground-truth diagnostic state and §23.2 treats
terminating 'unknown' under insufficient evidence as a
success. Do NOT interpret as confirmation of H5.
adjudication.transparency: This is post-experiment adjudication of an underspecified
selection term; NOT a preregistered metric definition.
adjudication.h5_status: unsupported/falsified with respect to its concrete
attribution prediction; NOT retroactively re-scored as D won

note: Both rankings are preserved and NOT collapsed into one claim.
Settlement (CEP) semantics are NOT altered; Settlement is not
synonymous with success. The §23.1 result is evidence that
retrieval representation may affect two separable capabilities
(attribution power; epistemic restraint/abstention), to be tested
as a new hypothesis later, not a conclusion already established.
